summary: ALT is an enzyme concentrated inside liver cells. When those cells are irritated or damaged it leaks into the blood, which makes ALT the most liver-specific of the routine liver enzymes.
what_it_measures: The activity of alanine aminotransferase in blood, reported in U/L.

interpretations.meaning: A raised ALT indicates liver cell irritation. Mild persistent elevations are most often fatty liver; sudden large rises suggest acute injury.

when_to_seek_help: If a raised ALT comes with yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine or severe abdominal pain, seek medical attention the same day.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
